title: Token provenance & retcon policy for streaming -> tool-call mismatch reconciliation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When proxying OpenAI Responses-style streaming while supporting Redwood's tool/function calling primitives we see rare but customer-visible mismatches: partially emitted tokens that later become part of a tool call invocation, or tool-call signals arriving out-of-order relative to streamed chunks. These cases cause incorrect tool routing, silent data loss, and operator confusion. Goal: Design and implement a lightweight token-provenance and retcon policy that enables runtime reconciliation of streamed token chunks with tool/function-call intents, with clear auditability and safe fallback semantics for legacy clients.
comments: 2025-02-19: Triage meeting notes — replicable cases identified from runner logs (3 customer incidents). Decided to prioritize deterministic reconciliation over opportunistic heuristics.

2025-02-22: Spike completed — micro-benchmark shows ~1.8% of streams contain token/tool boundaries crossing chunk frames for our top-5 workloads. Prototype uses per-request token offsets + provisional tool-call markers.

2025-02-26: Design review with PM/Infra — agreed to three-layer approach: (1) token provenance header attached to each stream frame, (2) retcon handler in gateway that can rewrite tool-call boundaries up to N tokens back, (3) telemetry + safe fallback to non-retcon path if latency SLO would be violated.
2025-03-01: PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/rw-runtime/pull/7812) implementing frame headers + gateway reconciler. Initial unit tests added for canonical cases.

2025-03-04: QA report — found regression when KV-cache reuse is high: retcon rewrites collided with cached prefix lengths. Added a guard to disable retcon when cache-hit ratio > 80% until deterministic cache alignment invariant is implemented.

2025-03-06: Security review requested — retcon introduces a temporary buffer of emitted tokens; confirm no additional PII retention beyond existing streaming window. Security requested threat model doc link (see links).
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler can detect and correct tool-call boundaries when a tool invocation marker is found within the previous N=16 tokens of the last emitted chunk
End-to-end tests covering: split-token tool-call start, tool-call marker emitted then retracted, and out-of-order marker arrival
Telemetry emits per-request reconciliation outcome with breakdown (no-op, retcon-applied, fallback-disabled) and latency impact
Runtime includes a safe-guard to disable retcon for requests that would violate the per-request latency budget
Documentation updated: Console runbook + API compatibility note describing retcon semantics and expected behaviors for legacy clients
